title: Marathas – The Protectors of the Nation

facts.text: After Bajirao I, Shahu Maharaj appointed his son Balaji Bajirao alias Nanasaheb the Peshwa.
facts.quote: After Bajirao I, Shahu Maharaj appointed his son Balaji Bajirao alias Nanasaheb the Peshwa.

facts.text: The region to the north-west of Ayodhya province at the foothills of the Himalayas was called Rohilkhand in the 18th century.
facts.quote: The region to the north-west of Ayodhya province at the foothills of the Himalayas was called Rohilkhand in the 18th century.

facts.text: The Pathans who had migrated from Afghanistan and settled in Rohilkhand were known as Rohillas.
facts.quote: The Pathans who had migrated from Afghanistan had settled in this region. They were known as Rohillas.

facts.text: The Rohillas wrought havoc in the Doab of the Ganga and Yamuna; the Nawab of Ayodhya invited the Marathas, who chastised the Rohillas.
facts.quote: The Rohillas had wrought havoc in the Doab region of the Ganga and Yamuna rivers. The Nawab of Ayodhya invited the Marathas to subdue the Rohillas. The Marathas chastised the Rohillas.

facts.text: Ahmadshah Abdali, the ruler of Afghanistan, marched on the Punjab in 1751 CE.
facts.quote: Ahmadshah Abdali, the ruler of Afghanistan, was attracted by the riches of India. He marched on the Punjab in 1751 CE.

facts.text: The Emperor entered into a treaty with the Marathas in April 1752.
facts.quote: Therefore, the Emperor entered into a treaty with the Marathas in April 1752.

facts.text: By the treaty the Marathas agreed to protect the Mughal power from the Rohillas, the Jats, the Rajputs and the Afghans.
facts.quote: According to this treaty, the Marathas agreed to protect the Mughal power from enemies like the Rohillas, the Jats, the Rajputs and the Afghans.

facts.text: In return the Marathas were to get cash, the right to collect chauthai in the Punjab, Multan, Rajputana, Sindh and Rohilkhand, and the Subhedari of Ajmer and Agra provinces.
facts.quote: In return, the Marathas were to get cash money, the right to collect chauthai in the territories of the Punjab, Multan, Rajputana, Sindh and Rohilkhand and the Subhedari of Ajmer and Agra provinces.

facts.text: The Peshwa sent the Shinde-Holkar armies to protect Delhi; learning this, Abdali went back to his country.
facts.quote: As per the treaty, the Peshwa sent the Shinde-Holkar armies for the protection of Delhi on behalf of the Chhatrapati. When Abdali learnt that the Marathas were marching to Delhi, he went back to his country.

facts.text: The Emperor gave the Marathas Chauthai rights to Mughal subhas including Kabul, Kandahar and Peshawar, which were then part of Abdali's Afghanistan.
facts.quote: the Emperor gave them Chauthai rights to the Mughal subhas. These subhas included Kabul, Kandahar and Peshawar. ... now they were part of Abdali's Afghanistan.

facts.text: Raghunathrao, brother of Peshwa Nanasaheb, with Jayappa Shinde and Malharrao Holkar, undertook the campaign of North India to combat Abdali.
facts.quote: Raghunathrao, brother of the Peshwa Nanasaheb, accompanied by Jayappa Shinde and Malharrao Holkar, undertook the campaign of North India to combat Abdali.

facts.text: Surajmal Jat and Rani Kishori were the only ones who helped the Marathas wounded in the battle of Panipat.
facts.quote: Surajmal Jat and Rani Kishori were the only ones who helped the Marathas wounded in the battle of Panipat.

facts.text: Some orthodox sects in the North persuaded Abdali to invade, expecting him to drive the Marathas back to the South, beyond the river Narmada.
facts.quote: They persuaded Abdali to invade India with a view to reducing the Maratha might. They expected that Abdali would defeat the Marathas and drive them away back to the South, beyond the river Narmada.

facts.text: Najibkhan, a Rohilla chief, could not tolerate Maratha supremacy; at his behest Abdali invaded India for the fifth time and captured Delhi.
facts.quote: Najibkhan was a Rohilla chief. He found it hard to tolerate the Maratha supremacy in the North. At the behest of Najibkhan, Abdali invaded India again. This was the fifth time he had invaded India. He captured Delhi.

facts.text: Raghunathrao and Malharrao Holkar recaptured Delhi and the Punjab, and the Marathas pursued Abdali's soldiers up to Attock in 1758 CE, where the Maratha standard was raised.
facts.quote: The Marathas pursued Abdali's soldiers right up to Attock in 1758 CE. The Maratha standard was raised at Attock.

facts.text: Attock is in present day Pakistan; from Attock the Marathas pushed the campaign up to Peshawar.
facts.quote: Attock is in present day Pakistan. From Attock, the Marathas pushed the campaign up to Peshawar.

facts.text: To crush Najibkhan the Peshwa sent Dattaji Shinde and Janakoji Shinde to the North; Najibkhan kept Dattaji engaged in negotiations and called Abdali.
facts.quote: the Peshwa sent Dattaji Shinde and Janakoji Shinde to the North. ... Keeping Dattaji engaged in negotiations, Najibkhan established contacts with Abdali.

facts.text: Dattaji and Abdali confronted each other at Buradi Ghat on the banks of the Yamuna, where Dattaji met with a heroic death.
facts.quote: Dattaji and Abdali confronted each other at Buradi Ghat on the banks of the Yamuna. A fierce fight ensued. Dattaji showed tremendous valour. He met with a heroic death in this battle.

facts.text: Qutub Shah, adviser of Najib Khan Rohilla, asked the wounded Dattaji if he would fight more, and Dattaji replied with pride.
facts.quote: Najib Khan Rohilla's adviser Qutub Shah stepped down from his elephant and came towards Dattaji. ... he replied with pride

facts.text: Nanasaheb sent his cousin Sadashivraobhau and his eldest son Vishwasrao to the North to crush Abdali; Sadashivraobhau was Chimajiappa's son.
facts.quote: Nanasaheb sent his cousin Sadashivraobhau and eldest son Vishwasrao to the North to crush Abdali. Sadashivraobhau was Chimajiappa's son.

facts.text: Ibrahimkhan Gardi, chief of the artillery, had defeated the Nizam in the battle of Udgir in 1760 CE.
facts.quote: Ibrahimkhan Gardi was the chief of the artillery. He had defeated the Nizam in the battle of Udgir in 1760 CE, on the strength of this artillery.

facts.text: On 14 January 1761 the Marathas opened the Third Battle of Panipat by attacking Abdali's army.
facts.quote: On 14 January 1761, the Marathas opened the battle by attacking Abdali's army. This was the Third Battle of Panipat.

facts.text: At Panipat Vishwasrao fell to an enemy bullet, Sadashivraobhau disappeared in the battle fray, and the Marathas were defeated.
facts.quote: Vishwasrao fell a victim to an enemy bullet in the battle. ... He disappeared in the battle fray. ... The Marathas were defeated.

facts.text: Approximately 1,50,000 people were killed in the battle of Panipat.
facts.quote: Approximately 1,50,000 people were killed in the battle of Panipat.

facts.text: The Marathas fought at Panipat with the broad perspective that India is for Indians.
facts.quote: The Marathas fought at Panipat with the broad perspective that India is for Indians.

facts.text: The Marathas were the first in history to realise that India was one country.
facts.quote: We can say that the Marathas were the first in our history to realise that India was one country

facts.text: After the death of Peshwa Nanasaheb, his son Madhavrao succeeded him as Peshwa.
facts.quote: After the death of Peshwa Nanasaheb, his son Madhavrao succeeded him to the office of the Peshwa.

facts.text: Madhavrao defeated the Nizam at Rakshasbhuvan near Paithan.
facts.quote: Madhavrao defeated the Nizam at Rakshasbhuvan near Paithan.

facts.text: The Marathas defeated Hyder Ali, the Sultan of Mysore, at Moti Talav near Srirangapattan; he ceded the region north of the river Tungabhadra.
facts.quote: Hyder Ali was the Sultan of Mysore. ... The Marathas defeated Hyder in a battle at Moti Talav near Srirangapattan. He then agreed to cede the region north of the river Tungabhadra to the Marathas.

facts.text: Peshwa Madhavrao died in 1772 CE; his death was an irreparable loss to the Maratha State.
facts.quote: Peshwa Madhavrao died in 1772 CE. ... The death of this capable Peshwa was an irreparable loss to the Maratha State.

facts.text: Madhavrao dug many wells in Pune, reformed the judiciary, started artillery and ammunition factories and established a mint; Nana Phadnavis and Ramshastri Prabhune emerged under his rule.
facts.quote: He dug many wells in Pune and increased the water supply to the city. Administrators like Nana Phadnavis and judges like Ramshastri Prabhune emerged under his rule. ... He also established a mint to make coins.

facts.text: Narayanrao and Sawai Madhavrao, the Peshwas after Madhavrao, did not live long; Raghunathrao sought shelter with the British, leading to war.
facts.quote: The two Peshwas who succeeded Peshwa Madhavrao, namely Narayanrao and Sawai Madhavrao, did not live long. ... Raghunathrao, who had once raised the Maratha standard at Attock, sought shelter with the British to satisfy his greed for power.

facts.text: Hyder Ali died in 1782 CE and his son Tipu became the Sultan of Mysore.
facts.quote: Hyder Ali died in 1782 CE. After him his son Tipu became the Sultan of Mysore.

facts.text: Tipu was a skilled warrior, a scholar and a poet who established contact with the French.
facts.quote: He was a skilled warrior, a scholar and a poet. ... He established contact with French and shook the foundation of British supremacy.

facts.text: Tipu died in 1799 CE in a battle against the British.
facts.quote: He died in 1799 CE in a battle against the British.

facts.text: Madhavrao sent Mahadji Shinde, Tukoji Holkar, Ramchandra Kanade and Visajipant Biniwale to re-establish Maratha rule in the North.
facts.quote: Madhavrao dispatched Mahadji Shinde, Tukoji Holkar, Ramchandra Kanade and Visajipant Biniwale to re-establish the Maratha rule in the North.

facts.text: The Maratha army defeated the Jats, Rohillas and Rajputs and restored Emperor Shah Alam to the throne of Delhi under Maratha protection.
facts.quote: The Maratha army defeated the Jats, the Rohillas and the Rajputs. The Marathas restored the Emperor Shah Alam to the throne of Delhi under their own protection.

facts.text: Abdali or his descendants never invaded India again; they sent a messenger to Pune to establish cordial relations.
facts.quote: Abdali or his descendants did not muster enough courage to invade India again. ... They sent a messenger to Pune to establish cordial relations.

facts.text: Malharrao Holkar, Ahilyabai Holkar and Mahadji Shinde had a lion's share in reviving Maratha supremacy in the North.
facts.quote: Malharrao Holkar, Ahilyabai Holkar and Mahadji Shinde had a lion's share in all this.

facts.text: In the Peshwa family tree, Nanasaheb's sons were Vishwasrao, Madhavrao (Peshwa), Yeshwantrao and Narayanrao (Peshwa); Sawai Madhavrao was Narayanrao's son.
facts.quote: Vishwasrao  Madhavrao (Peshwa)  Yeshwantrao  Narayanrao (Peshwa) ... Sawai Madhavrao (Peshwa)
